payload.reason: The evidence indicates that in the UCCA scheme, a node can represent either a terminal or a non-terminal, but not both simultaneously, as they serve different roles in the semantic representation.

claims.text: A node in the UCCA scheme can be either a terminal or a non-terminal, but not both at the same time.
UCCA nodes correspond to either single tokens (terminals) or multiple tokens viewed as a single entity (non-terminals).
The UCCA scheme uses non-terminal nodes to represent complex semantic units, indicating that nodes can be classified distinctly as terminal or non-terminal.
